title.zh: 平均数、中位数与离散程度

clips.send: Five friends count the books they read this month: 2, 7, 4, 3 and 9. One read a lot, one read very little. What single number fairly describes the “typical” amount?
clips.text: Five friends count the books they read this month: 2, 7, 4, 3 and 9. One read a lot, one read very little. What single number fairly describes the “typical” amount?

clips.send: For a bigger data set, split it into quarters. Eleven quiz scores: the median is the 6th score, 7. The median of the lower half is Q1 equals 6 ; of the upper half, Q3 equals 9 . A box plot draws these, and the interquartile range is IQR equals Q3 minus Q1 equals 3 .
clips.text: For a bigger data set, split it into quarters. Eleven quiz scores: the median is the 6th score, 7. The median of the lower half is Q 1 = 6; of the upper half, Q 3 = 9. A box plot draws these, and the interquartile range is IQR = Q 3 - Q 1 = 3.

clips.send: Suppose the friend who read 9 actually read 19. The heavy side tips the balance, and the mean has to slide right to 7 to balance again. The median? Still 4. An outlier pulls the mean, but barely moves the median.
clips.text: Suppose the friend who read 9 actually read 19. The heavy side tips the balance, and the mean has to slide right to 7 to balance again. The median? Still 4. An outlier pulls the mean, but barely moves the median.

clips.send: Idea: share the books out evenly. Move books from tall stacks to short ones until every stack is level. Everyone ends up with 5, because the total, 25 , split 5 ways is 25 divided by 5 equals 5 . That level is the mean.
clips.text: Idea: share the books out evenly. Move books from tall stacks to short ones until every stack is level. Everyone ends up with 5, because the total, 25, split 5 ways is 25 div 5 = 5. That level is the mean.

clips.send: Try it with 4, 8, 6, 5, 7. Mean: 30 divided by 5 equals 6 . In order 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, so the median is 6. Range: 8 minus 4 equals 4 . MAD: (2 plus 1 plus 0 plus 1 plus 2) divided by 5 equals 1.2 .
clips.text: Try it with 4, 8, 6, 5, 7. Mean: 30 div 5 = 6. In order 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, so the median is 6. Range: 8 - 4 = 4. MAD: (2 + 1 + 0 + 1 + 2) div 5 = 1.2.

clips.send: The median is the middle value once the data are in order. Cross off one value from each end, again and again: 2 and 9, then 3 and 7. The one left, 4, is the median. (With an even number of values, take the halfway point of the two middle ones.)
clips.text: The median is the middle value once the data are in order. Cross off one value from each end, again and again: 2 and 9, then 3 and 7. The one left, 4, is the median. (With an even number of values, take the halfway point of the two middle ones.)

clips.send: Center is not the whole story; we also want spread. The range is max minus min: 9 minus 2 equals 7 . The mean absolute deviation (MAD) is the average distance from the mean: line the distances up, 3 plus 2 plus 1 plus 2 plus 4 equals 12 , then share them out, 12 divided by 5 equals 2.4 .
clips.text: Center is not the whole story; we also want spread. The range is max − min: 9 - 2 = 7. The mean absolute deviation (MAD) is the average distance from the mean: line the distances up, 3+2+1+2+4 = 12, then share them out, 12 div 5 = 2.4.

clips.send: So there are two kinds of summary. Measures of center describe a typical value: the mean and the median. Measures of spread (variability) describe how far the data stretch: the range, the IQR and the MAD.
clips.text: So there are two kinds of summary. Measures of center describe a typical value: the mean and the median. Measures of spread (variability) describe how far the data stretch: the range, the IQR and the MAD.

clips.send: Now put the same data on a number line as a dot plot. The mean is also the balance point: the distances on the left ( 3 plus 2 plus 1 equals 6 ) exactly match the distances on the right ( 2 plus 4 equals 6 ), so the line balances at 5.

clips.send: 把同样的数据画在数轴上，成为点图。平均数还是“平衡点”：左边各点到 5 的距离之和（ 3 加 2 加 1 等于 6 ）正好等于右边各点的距离之和（ 2 加 4 等于 6 ），所以数轴在 5 处保持平衡。
clips.text: 把同样的数据画在数轴上，成为点图。平均数还是“平衡点”：左边各点到 5 的距离之和（3 + 2 + 1 = 6）正好等于右边各点的距离之和（2 + 4 = 6），所以数轴在 5 处保持平衡。

clips.send: 练一练：数据 4、8、6、5、7。平均数： 30 除以 5 等于 6 。排序后是 4、5、6、7、8，中位数是 6。极差： 8 减 4 等于 4 。平均绝对偏差： (2 加 1 加 0 加 1 加 2) 除以 5 等于 1.2 。
五个朋友统计了这个月各自读了几本书：2、7、4、3、9。有人读得多，有人读得少。用哪一个数来代表“一般水平”才公平？
clips.text: 五个朋友统计了这个月各自读了几本书：2、7、4、3、9。有人读得多，有人读得少。用哪一个数来代表“一般水平”才公平？

clips.send: 只看“中心”还不够，还要看数据有多分散。极差 等于 最大值减最小值： 9 减 2 等于 7 。平均绝对偏差（MAD）是各数据到平均数距离的平均值：把距离首尾相接， 3 加 2 加 1 加 2 加 4 等于 12 ，再平均分： 12 除以 5 等于 2.4 。
clips.text: 只看“中心”还不够，还要看数据有多分散。极差 = 最大值 − 最小值：9 - 2 = 7。平均绝对偏差（MAD）是各数据到平均数距离的平均值：把距离首尾相接，3+2+1+2+4 = 12，再平均分：12 div 5 = 2.4。

clips.send: 数据多的时候，可以把它分成四份。11 个测验成绩：中位数是第 6 个，等于 7。下半部分的中位数是下四分位数 Q1 等于 6 ，上半部分的中位数是上四分位数 Q3 等于 9 。箱线图把它们画出来，四分位距 IQR 等于 Q3 减 Q1 等于 3 。
clips.text: 数据多的时候，可以把它分成四份。11 个测验成绩：中位数是第 6 个，等于 7。下半部分的中位数是下四分位数 Q 1 = 6，上半部分的中位数是上四分位数 Q 3 = 9。箱线图把它们画出来，四分位距 IQR = Q 3 - Q 1 = 3。

clips.send: 所以有两类统计量。集中趋势的度量描述“典型值”：平均数和中位数。离散程度的度量描述数据有多分散：极差、四分位距（IQR）和平均绝对偏差（MAD）。
clips.text: 所以有两类统计量。集中趋势的度量描述“典型值”：平均数和中位数。离散程度的度量描述数据有多分散：极差、四分位距（IQR）和平均绝对偏差（MAD）。

clips.send: 假如读了 9 本的那位其实读了 19 本。重的一边把数轴压歪了，平均数必须向右移到 7 才能重新平衡。中位数呢？还是 4。离群值会把平均数拉过去，却几乎拉不动中位数。
clips.text: 假如读了 9 本的那位其实读了 19 本。重的一边把数轴压歪了，平均数必须向右移到 7 才能重新平衡。中位数呢？还是 4。离群值会把平均数拉过去，却几乎拉不动中位数。

clips.send: 把数据从小到大排好，正中间的那个数就是中位数。从两端同时各划掉一个：先划掉 2 和 9，再划掉 3 和 7，剩下的 4 就是中位数。（如果数据个数是偶数，就取中间两个数的平均数。）

clips.send: 想法：把书平均分。从高的书堆搬到矮的书堆，直到每堆一样高。每人最后都是 5 本，因为总数 25 平均分给 5 人： 25 除以 5 等于 5 。这个高度就是平均数。
